items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the real property tax law, in relation to extending certain
deadlines related to a tax abatement for certain alterations and improvements
to multiple dwellings
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8170

SPONSOR: KAVANAGH
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the real property tax law, in relation to extending
certain deadlines related to a tax abatement for certain alterations and
improvements to multiple dwellings

 
PURPOSE:

This bill would extend the completion date required for securing abate-
ment of taxation for certain alterations and improvements to multiple
dwellings to June 30, 2030 and gives until June 30, 2026 for local
legislative bodies to adopt this extension through local laws or ordi-
nances.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends clase (c) of subparagraph 10 of paragraph (a) of subdi-
vision 21 of section 489 of the Real Property Tax Law to extend the
project completion date in order to be eligible for the Affordable Hous-
ing Rehabilitation Program tax abatement from June 30, 2026 to June 30,
2030.

Section 1 also amends the opening paragraph of paragraph (I)) of subdi-
vision 21 of section 489 of the Real Property Tax Law to set June 30,
2026 as the date by which local legislative bodies may enact the project
complete date extension through local laws or ordinances.

Section 2 sets forth the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

In 2023, the legislature passed, and the Governor signed into law, a tax
abatement program called the Affordable Housing Rehabilitation Program
to succeed the expired, former J-51 Program to incentivize a variety of
alterations and improvements in multifamily buildings, including the
installation or replacement of heating systems, plumbing, wiring, eleva-
tors, windows and a range of other major capital improvements.

The Affordable Housing Rehabilitation Program was designed as a targeted
program, with a simplified tax-abatement formula, to more effectively
direct benefits to encourage affordability of safe and healthy dwell-
ings.

The program extends tax abatements to rental buildings that meet
prescribed affordable rent levels and tenant income restrictions for
rentals upon vacancy during the restriction period. Other protections
are built-in for tenants of affordable rental units, such as a private
right of action for owner violations of the program requirements. Even
more critically, during the restriction period, the owner of any such
eligible rental building must waive the collection of any rent adjust-
ment granted by the State Division of Housing and Community Renewal
pursuant to rent regulation that is attributable to eligible
construction for which such eligible rental building receives program
benefits.


On December 5, 2024, the New York City Council passed Intro 654-2024 to
adopt this new tax abatement program. It was signed into law as Local
Law 122 of 2024 on December 18, 2024.

This bill seeks to address the limitation that the current law's fast
approaching project completion deadline of June 30, 2026 poses as a
challenge for prospective applicants of the program to conduct qualify-
ing repairs and environmental upgrades in time to secure the tax abate-
ment. Particularly for buildings that need to work towards energy effi-
ciency and decarbonization compliance in accordance with New York City's
Local Law 97, which may involve extensive multisystem upgrades, some
projects would be very difficult to scope, finance, and start and
complete within the 1.5 year window that owners effectively have between
the enactment of Local Law 122 and the program's June 2026 project
completion date.

Extending the project completion date by four years to June 30, 2030 and
giving local legislative bodies until June 30, 2026 to enact local laws
or ordinances to adopt this extension, will enable more property owners
to access the tax incentives offered under the Affordable Housing Reha-
bilitation Program.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

This is a new bill.

S4709A Kavanagh / A7758 Braunstein of 2023 (Chapter 536 of 2023) author-
ized the program for construction completed by the current June 30, 2026
deadline.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None to the state.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

A.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the real property tax law, in relation to authorizing a tax
abatement for alterations and improvements to multiple dwellings for purposes
of preserving habitability in affordable housing
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8170A

SPONSOR: KAVANAGH
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the real property tax law, in relation to authorizing a
tax abatement for alterations and improvements to multiple dwellings for
purposes of preserving habitability in affordable housing

 
PURPOSE:

This bill creates a new version of New York City's property tax abate-
ment program for renovating a residential apartment building, commonly
known as J-51.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

This bill was introduced in 2025 to extend the completion date required
for securing abatement of taxation for certain alterations and improve-
ments to multiple dwellings to June 30, 2030 and gives until June 30,
2026 for local legislative bodies to adopt this extension through local
laws or ordinances.

The amendment (S8170A) expands on the extension by including additional
changes to J-51, all as a new subdivision to Section 489 of the Real
Property Tax Law.

Section 1 of the bill amends Section 489 of the Real Property Tax Law by
adding a new subdivision 22 that would establish an updated J-51 tax
abatement program for renovating apartment buildings in New York City.

Subsection (a) of the new subdivision 22 sets forth definitions of
terms, with the following terms defined differently under this bill from
the same terms defined in the current J-51R program (Real Property Tax
Law subdivision 21) and/or in the FY 2026-2027 Executive Budget in ELFA
Part 0 (S9006) ("Executive Budget Proposal"):  This bill and the Execu-
tive Budget Proposal adds the definition for "Area median income" as the
income limits as defined annually by the United States department of
housing and urban development for the New York City area.

"Certified reasonable cost schedule" -- Under this bill, the local hous-
ing agency is directed to update the certified reasonable cost schedule
every two years. In the Executive Budget Proposal, updates are required
every three years. Under J-51R certified reasonable cost schedules are
"updated as necessary."

"Eligible construction" -- Under this bill and in the Executive Budget
Proposal, eligible construction must have a completion date that is
after June 30, 2026 and prior to June 30, 2036 and no more than 30
months after the project's work commencement date. Under J-51R, the
completion date of an eligible construction must be prior to June 30,
2026 and no more than 30 months after the project's work commencement
date.

"Eligible rental building" -- This bill adds buildings in which 90% or
more of the total number of dwelling units are subject to rent regu-
lation as an eligible rental building. Neither the Executive Budget
Proposal nor J-51R includes this housing type as an eligible rental
building.
"Homeownership average assessed valuation limitation" -- Under this
bill, an eligible homeownership building must have an average assessed
valuation that does not exceed $75,000 per dwelling unit, and this valu-
ation shall be adjusted annually to reflect Consumer Prince Index
increases. The Executive Budget Proposal sets the average assessed valu-
ation limitation at $60,000. The current average assessed valuation
limitation under J-51R is $45,000.

Subsection (b) of the new subdivision 22 describes the J-51 abatement
that eligible buildings can receive. J-51 would abate existing real
estate taxes by up to 8 1/3 percent, annually, of the cost of the
approved eligible work for up to 20 years. The amount of abatement
received for a given twelve-month period cannot exceed the total amount
of real property taxes the building is assessed for that same period.
This amount is further restricted for eligible rental buildings owned by
a limited-profit housing company or a redevelopment company and for an
eligible homeownership building (regulated and unregulated), where the
abatement cannot exceed 50% the total amount of real property taxes the
building is assessed during the applicable twelve-month period.

This bill provides that eligible buildings may recover up to 100% of
certified reasonable costs approved for the abatement. This is an
increase from up to 70% of certified reasonable costs under the current
J-51R program, and the same increase as proposed in the FY 2026-2027
Executive Budget in ELFA Part 0 (S9006).

This bill further provides for the J-51 application fee to also be a
recoverable cost. Neither J-51R nor the Executive Budget Proposal
permits application fees to be recoverable.  Subsection (c) of the new
subdivision 22 directs each agency or department involved in the admin-
istration of J-51 to adopt and promulgate rules, regulations, and docu-
ments. This bill does not require local action by the city of New York
to adopt the new J-51 program, which is needed for the current J-51R
program. The Executive Budget Proposal also does not require local
adoption.

Subsection (d) of the new subdivision 22 sets forth the application
process, including the timeline for submitting an application for a
certificate of eligibility and reasonable cost, documentation and mate-
rials that applicants need to provide, application fee, process for
remedying a deficient application, and additional requirements and
compliance that the local administrator may require.

This bill sets the J-51 application fee at $75 per dwelling unit with a
cap of $20,000 and, for approved projects, allows the amount paid for
the application fee to be included in the aggregate total that may be
abated. The Executive Budget Proposal leaves in place J-51R's current
fee structure of $1,000 for the first 6 units of a building and $75 for
each additional isn't without a cap.  The provision in this subsection
to permit the administering agency to require an applicant to demon-
strate compliance with the housing maintenance code is new in this bill
and in the Executive Budget Proposal.

Subsection (e) of the new subdivision 22 lays out additional require-
ments for eligible buildings other than one owned and operated by a
limited-profit housing company. This is unchanged from current J-51R
requirements.

Subsection (e) also specifies that while an owner must file a waiver
foregoing Major Capital Improvement benefits for the same work being
claimed for J-51 benefits, that such a waiver does not have to be filed
until after the building's J-51 application has been approved.  The
prescribed timing for filing the waiver is new in this bill and in the
Executive Budget Proposal.

Subsection (f) of the new subdivision 22 requires compliance with all
applicable law as a condition of receiving J-51 benefits. This is
unchanged from current J-5 1R requirements.

Subsection (g) of the new subdivision 22 adds tenant notification
requirements. Owners must give tenants notice between 30-180 days before
the commencement of work, specifying the work to be done, the identity
and contact information of the building representative, and information
on tenants' rights under applicable law. These provisions are new and
the same in both this bill and in the Executive Budget Proposal.

Subsection (h) of the new subdivision 22 adds the requirement that an
owner must submit a notice of intent with the administering housing
agency. This is a new requirement and is the same in both this bill and
in the Executive Budget Proposal.

Subsection (i) of the new subdivision 22 adds the provision that upon
issuance of a certificate of eligibility and reasonable cost and payment
of outstanding fees, the administering housing agency (NYC Department of
Housing Preservation and Development / HID) shall be authorized to tran-
smit the certificate to the local tax agency (NYC Department of Finance
/ DOF), and DOF shall certify the amount of taxes to be abated. This is
a new provision and is the same in both this bill and in the Executive
Budget Proposal.

Subsection (j) of the new subdivision 22 specifies program ineligibility
for 1) buildings with outstanding property taxes or PILOT, and buildings
with outstanding water and sewer arrears owed as of the last day of the
tax period preceding the date of the receipt of the certificate of
eligibility and reasonable cost; and 2) buildings with property tax or
water and sewer arrears due at any time during the J-51 benefits term
that remain unpaid for one year.  This is a current provision in J-51R
that both this bill and the Executive Budget Proposal leave unchanged.

Subsection (k) of the new subdivision 22 specifies additional limita-
tions on eligibility on receiving concurrent benefits, portioning bene-
fits for buildings with non-residential space, and applying benefits to
the building structure. These are current provisions in J-51R that both
this bill and the Executive Budget Proposal leave unchanged.

Subsection (1) of the new subdivision 22 sets forth reinspection penal-
ty. This is a current provision in J-51R that both this bill and the
Executive Budget Proposal leave unchanged.  Subsection (m) of the new
subdivision 22 sets forth strict liability for inaccurate applications.
This is a current provision in J-51R that both this bill and the Execu-
tive Budget Proposal leave unchanged.  Subsection (n) of the new subdi-
vision 22 adds a penalty of no more than $500 for anyone who knowingly
makes false statements or omissions to any material matter in an appli-
cation. This is a new requirement and is the same in both this bill and
in the Executive Budget Proposal.

Subsection (o) of the new subdivision 22 grants the local housing admin-
istrator authority to require access to information for the enforcement
of J-51 eligibility. This is a current provision in J-51R that both this
bill and the Executive Budget Proposal leave unchanged.  Subsection (p)
of the new subdivision 22 specifies that non-compliance can lead to
termination of benefits. This is a current provision in J-51R that both
this bill and the Executive Budget Proposal leave unchanged.

Subsection (q) of the new subdivision 22 sets forth criminal liability
for unauthorized uses in an eligible building's dwelling units. This is
a current provision in J-51R that both this bill and the Executive Budg-
et Proposal leave unchanged.

Subsection (r) of the new subdivision 22 grants private right of action
to prospective, present, or former tenants to pursue action against the
violation of program requirements and prohibitions. This is a current
provision in J-51R that both this bill and the Executive Budget Proposal
leave unchanged.

Subsection (s) of the new subdivision 22 authorizes the administering
housing agency to make application for the appointment of a receiver for
a non-compliant building. This is a current provision in J-51R that both
this bill and the Executive Budget Proposal leave unchanged.  Subsection
(t) of the new subdivision 22 adds reporting requirements.  Two years
after the effective date and annually thereafter, HPD in consultation
with DOF shall submit reports to the Mayor, Speaker of the New York City
Council, and make the report publicly available on its website. This is
a new requirement and is the same in both this bill and in the Executive
Budget Proposal.

Subsection (u) of the new subdivision 22 requires HPD to take into
consideration requirements imposed by New York City's local laws includ-
ing LL 11 (fa§ ade inspection and repair), LL97 (reducing buildings'
greenhouse gas emissions), and the impacts of inflation when updating
the program's certified reasonable cost schedule. This is a new require-
ment and is the same in both this bill and in the Executive Budget
Proposal.

Section 2 of the bill sets forth the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

In 2023, the State enacted a law authorizing the City of New York to
adopt a tax abatement program called the Affordable Housing Rehabili-
tation Program, known as 3-51R, to succeed the expired, former 3-51
Program, to incentivize a variety of alterations and improvements in
multifamily buildings, including the installation or replacement of
heating systems, plumbing, wiring, elevators, windows and a range of
other major capital improvements. J-51R was designed as a targeted
program to more effectively direct benefits to promote affordable, safe,
well-maintained, environmentally sustainable dwellings.

On December 5, 2024, the New York City Council passed Intro 654-2024 to
adopt this new tax abatement program. It was signed into law as Local
Law 122 of 2024 on December 18, 2024, nearly a year-and-a-half after
State authorization, which has limited the opportunity for property
owners to benefit from the program.  This bill seeks to extend the
program for a decade beyond J-51R's fast-approaching project completion
deadline of June 30, 2026.  Particularly for buildings that need to work
towards energy efficiency and decarbonization in compliance with New
York City's Local Law 97, which may involve extensive multisystem
upgrades, many projects would be effectively impossible to scope,
finance, start and complete by the current deadline.

Extending the project completion date to June 30, 2036 and removing the
requirement for local adoption will enable more property owners to
access the tax incentive.

The FY 2026-2027 Executive Budget also proposes an extension of the
program, as well as a range of changes in the way it works. The Execu-
tive version would:

- Remove the requirement that New York City must adopt a new 3-51
program via Local Law;

- Increase the average assessed value cap for eligible homeownership
buildings;

- Direct NYC Department of Housing Preservation and Development to
update the Certified Reasonable Cost Schedule at regular intervals;

- Allow property owners to recover 100% of certified reasonable costs;

- Require applicants to demonstrate compliance with the NYC Housing
Maintenance Code;

- Resolve a previous 3-51R issue where proposed projects irrevocably
waived the option of applying for Major Capital Improvement charges to
cover the cost of improvements, even though their 3-51 application might
be disapproved;

- Set tenant notification requirements;

- Require applicants to file a notice of intent;

- Facilitate the sharing of information between HPD and DOF for imple-
menting the tax abatement;

- Add penalty for knowingly making false statements or omissions in the
application; and

- Add reporting requirements.  This bill adopts many of the reforms in
the Executive Budget Proposal and includes different and additional
provisions based on feedback received from engaging with a broad range
of stakeholders on ways to improve J-51. This bill would:

- Further raise the average assessed value cap and tie the cap to annual
CPI increases thereafter; - Expand the program to buildings with 90% or
more of total dwelling units subject to rent regulation;

- Increase the frequency of updates to the Certified Reasonable Cost
Schedule to every two years to better reflect material and labor costs
of allowable works under J-51; and

- Lower the application fee and authorize the application fee of
approved projects to be included in the aggregate total amount of tax
abatement. This is intended to reduce the number of buildings that are
eligible for J-51 but may be deterred from applying due to prohibitive
application fees.

With the inclusion of J-51 updates proposed under this bill, more build-
ing and co-op and condo owners in New York City would be able to access
the resources they need to repair and upgrade their buildings into safe
and environmentally sustainable homes for their residents.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

S4709A (Kavanagh) would have extended J-51R's project completion dead-
line from June 30, 2026 to June 30, 2030. The bill passed the Senate in
2025.

S4709A Kavanagh / A7758 Braunstein of 2023 (Chapter 536 of 2023) author-
ized the program for construction completed by the current June 30, 2026
deadline and expanded the range of eligible project types.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None to the state.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Authorizes a tax abatement for alterations and improvements to multiple dwellings for purposes of preserving habitability in affordable housing.
